_provenance: TWO SYNTHETIC DRIFTS, ONE OF WHICH WAS MISTAKEN FOR REAL. Retitled 2026-08-30; the mechanism this proves is unchanged and every assertion here still holds. live-baseline.json with profile_social_metrics REMOVED and company_enricher ADDED. NEITHER edit describes reality, and the original wording here ("THE TWO REAL BUGS") was wrong in both directions. Measured against the running server on 2026-08-30: GET /api/v1/catalog returns total:68 and DOES list profile_social_metrics, and an unauthenticated POST to it returns 401 (route exists, behind auth) exactly like the enrich_company control; company_enricher is NOT in that list and an identical POST returns 404. So profile_social_metrics is live and was never missing, and company_enricher was never present. What misled the earlier reading is recorded below and is a real server-side defect worth reporting upstream: three live rows (clean_domain, enrich_company, find_website_by_company_name) carry next_steps prose telling the caller to feed results into company_enricher, so the server documents an endpoint its own catalog does not list and its own router 404s. Everything else is verbatim. The company_enricher row is RECONSTRUCTED: by 2026-08-30 the live catalog table no longer listed it, so there was nothing left to record — but the live enrich_company row still says in its own next_steps prose "feed it into email_finder, people_search, or company_enricher", which is the server referring to an endpoint its own catalog does not list. Both bugs are frozen here so the oracle is proven against them forever, whatever the live server or _lib/api-catalog.json does next.

tools.name: ai_enrich
tools.description: Run an LLM completion against the configured AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or Perplexity). Used for classification, extraction, summarization, etc.

provider.description: AI provider: openai, anthropic, gemini, or perplexity

prompt.description: Prompt template; use {{fieldName}} placeholders for dynamic values

model.description: Model override; defaults to provider default model

context.description: Key-value pairs used for {{placeholder}} substitution in the prompt

output_schema.description: JSON schema used to guide structured output when output_type is json

max_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens; defaults to provider default

use_web_search.description: Enable web search when supported by the selected provider

search_domain_filter.description: Perplexity only; limit search to specific domains

search_recency_filter.description: Perplexity only; filter by recency: day, week, month, year

example_input.prompt: Jane Smith — VP Sales at Acme — logistics SaaS, 200 employees
example_input.system_prompt: You are a B2B lead scorer. Return JSON matching the schema.

tools.next_steps: Returns {result: <text or parsed JSON>}. When output_type='json', the response is already parsed — no extra parsing needed.

tools.name: clean_domain

messy_url.description: URL or domain to normalize (e.g. https://www.Example.COM/page?q=1)

tools.next_steps: Returns domain. Feed into email_finder, company_enricher, or web_scrape.

tools.name: company_enricher
tools.description: Enrich a company domain with firmographics. RECONSTRUCTED, not recorded: this row is modelled on the live enrich_company row so the payload is realistic.

tools.name: enrich_profile
tools.description: Enrich a LinkedIn profile URL and return structured personal data: full name, headline, current role, company, location, industry, skills, education, and the LinkedIn URN needed for profile_activities. Cached ~24h by default (set useCache=false for fresh data).
tools.next_steps: Returns {entityUrn, firstname, lastname, company.name, company.website, headline, ...}. Feed entityUrn into profile_activities for the person's posts/comments/reactions, or pipe firstname/lastname + company.website into email_finder.

tools.name: enrich_profiles_bulk
tools.description: Bulk-enrich up to 50 LinkedIn profiles in a single call by entityUrn. 1 credit per RESULT returned, not per call — cheaper than calling enrich_profile in a loop when you have ≥10 URNs already.
tools.next_steps: Returns an array of profile records. Missing URNs are silently skipped — diff the input and output to detect misses. Use enrich_profile for single lookups under ~5 URNs.

tools.name: lead_search
tools.description: Search LinkedIn leads (people) using seniority, title, function, industry, geography, and company filters. Costs 10 + (0.5 * returned results) credits.

sales_nav_url.description: Full LinkedIn Sales Navigator search URL. May be combined with individual filters.

geo_ids.description: LinkedIn geo IDs or location names

seniority.description: Seniority labels resolved to LinkedIn seniorityLevelIds.

functions.description: Job function labels resolved to LinkedIn functionIds.

industries.description: Industry labels resolved to LinkedIn industryIds.

years_of_experience.description: Experience range labels resolved to LinkedIn yearsOfExperienceIds.

years_at_current_company.description: Tenure range labels resolved to LinkedIn yearsAtCurrentCompanyIds.

profile_languages.description: Profile language labels resolved to language codes.

current_companies.description: Current company LinkedIn URLs or IDs.

past_companies.description: Past company LinkedIn URLs or IDs.

recently_changed_jobs.description: Filter for people who recently changed jobs.

exclude_geo_ids.description: LinkedIn geo IDs or location names to exclude.

exclude_current_companies.description: Current company LinkedIn URLs or IDs to exclude.

exclude_past_companies.description: Past company LinkedIn URLs or IDs to exclude.

exclude_schools.description: School LinkedIn URLs or IDs to exclude.

page.description: Positive page number for pagination. Defaults to 1.

session_id.description: Optional unique ID used to keep pagination requests on the same scraping resource. Generate a random string (for example, a UUID) and send the same value with each page request

tools.next_steps: Feed results into email_finder or enrich_profile for contact data.

tools.name: people_search
tools.description: Search 700M+ indexed LinkedIn profiles by job title, seniority, industry, company, or location. Returns a paginated list of profile previews. 0.1 credits per result returned.
tools.next_steps: Feed linkedin_url values into enrich_profile for fuller records, or into email_finder with the company domain.

tools.name: phone_finder
tools.description: Find a mobile phone number from a LinkedIn profile URL. Returns the first match found across multiple providers.
tools.next_steps: Returns result.phone. Soft-fail means no mobile on file — do not retry with same inputs.

tools.name: profile_search
tools.description: Live LinkedIn profile search by name, title, current company, or keywords. Lower latency but smaller filter surface than people_search. 0.1 credits per result.

current_company.description: Company ID or LinkedIn URL; comma-separated for multiple

past_company.description: Past company ID or URL; comma-separated for multiple

school.description: School ID or URL; comma-separated for multiple

geo_id.description: LinkedIn Geo ID — overrides location; use geo_id_search to resolve

follower_of.description: Filter profiles following a LinkedIn profile. URL or ID. Comma-separated.

tools.next_steps: Returns a list of profile hits. When multiple people share a name, always pass currentCompany to disambiguate — otherwise take the top hit at your own risk.

tools.name: web_scrape
tools.description: Fetch the full HTML of a page, optionally also rendering Markdown. 2 credits per call. Use for contextual grounding before summarisation.

url.description: URL of the page to scrape

formats.description: Output formats to include (e.g. html, markdown, links)

tools.next_steps: Returns {html, markdown}. Pipe markdown into ai_enrich for summarisation.
